scope.object: the metallic acts L^m R^m and their ticks [[m,1],[1,0]] for m = 1..7; every hyperbolic A in SL(2,Z) with entries up to 7
scope.hypotheses: exact integer arithmetic; the structural level only (no frame computed on the rivals); SnapPy census names; the identity det(A -+ I) = 2 -+ tr A for det A = 1

claim_one_line: THE SELECTION TESTED BY CHANGING IT (P-831's rule, the author's question): the tick's structure (a prime frustrated level, the tick a square root of -1 on it, the hand as the parity of ticks plus undoings) holds for every odd metallic m with m^2 + 4 prime (1, 3, 5, 7) and fails for even m, so it does not single out the golden; what separates golden from bronze is the left-over (bronze: (Z/3)^2 in its root s464, Z/3 in its tick bundle m005). And SE1 is one condition with two readings: for a positive-trace hyperbolic act, torsion-free <=> tr = 3 <=> the frustrated level is 5 <=> (B997's bound) the level's group SL(2, Z/N) is no larger than 2I; the act's opposite -A exchanges the torsion order |2 - tr| with the level |2 + tr| (m004 against m003). Every selection rule on record picks the golden; SE1 stays POSTULATED. 0 of 19.
